written.myAnswer: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical objects equipped with sensors, software, and other technologies that connect and exchange data with other devices and systems over the internet.

IoT connects physical devices and systems to the digital world so they can collect and share data. Analysing that data can improve efficiency and services and create opportunities in areas such as healthcare, agriculture, and smart homes.

An IoT system includes sensors, devices, actuators, a network, and data analysis. Sensors collect information from the environment; the network carries data between connected devices and the internet; and analysis processes the data to provide insights or support decisions. Devices can use the data to perform tasks, while actuators produce physical outputs in response. Analysis may take place on a device, a server, or in the cloud.

IoT can make transportation safer and more efficient through connected vehicles, smart traffic lights, and real-time tracking. Other applications include smart buses, trains and roads, self-driving cars, and smart delivery systems.

IoT devices may collect and share sensitive personal information, creating risks of unwanted access, exposure, or misuse. Insecure devices and communications can also increase the risk of cyberattacks. Strong unique passwords, regular software and firmware updates, and encryption can help protect data and privacy.
